ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $5.00 no-show cancellation fee to the rider (original payment method) and record the cancellation as voided; no driver warning required on this record.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: the complaint ("...charged $5.00 for nothing"), the driver's statement and the two chat messages contain no threat, harassment, sexual remark, accident or dangerous-driving allegation. safety_concern = none.

Clause selection (NS-0): the driver cancelled and logged the reason as rider_no_show, so NS-1/NS-2 govern. The rider's "I came out a minute after" is her account of timing; the system records decide.

NS-1 conditions, checked against the record:
(i) Arrival — app event "driver_arrived" at 12:57:00; GPS at 12:57:00 is (1.2836, 103.860502), ~30 m from the Marina Bay Sands pickup point (1.2839, 103.8607). Within 200 m → satisfied. The driver's chat at 12:57:30 confirms presence.
(ii) Wait — free wait runs from the later of scheduled pickup time and arrival, i.e. from 12:57:00 (arrival; the record shows no separate scheduled time). Five minutes expire at 13:02:00. The driver cancelled at 13:03:00, i.e. after 6 minutes → satisfied on its face.
(iii) Contact — requires at least 1 in-app message AND at least 1 in-app call placed before cancelling. Messages: 12:57:30 and 13:02:50 → satisfied. Calls: a single call attempt at 12:58:30, unanswered (duration 0). Whether "made a call" requires the call to connect is not addressed in NS-1's text, and the record does not settle it; because the failure below is dispositive regardless, this element is treated as undetermined and not relied upon.
(iv) Continuous presence — this fails. GPS thinned to every 6th sample shows the vehicle stationary on Bayfront Avenue at ~1.9 km/h from 12:57:30 through 13:03:00, but at 12:57:30 the first stationary fix is at 1.283594, 103.860508 and the fixes drift between 1.283584 and 1.283614 lat / 103.860491–103.860517 lng — a spread of roughly 3–4 m, consistent with a parked vehicle, and all fixes remain within ~30 m of the pickup point. That supports continuous presence rather than contradicting it.

However, the free-wait computation is not the deciding problem — the record is missing a decisive piece of evidence. The telemetry is a thinned sample (19 of 109 points, every 6th sample, stated in the _note), so the 30-second gaps leave the vehicle's exact position and status between 12:57:00 and 13:03:00 unverifiable at 30-second granularity, and there is no full-resolution track to confirm the driver did not leave and return, nor any arrival auto-confirmation event. More importantly, the record contains no full waiting-fee basis (waiting_fee_basis is null) and no scheduled pickup time field against which the earlier of the wait start could be verified; the wait was counted only from the recorded arrival.

Weighing this: the record does not establish an NS-1 failure that would void the fee on the merits — the driver appears to have arrived, waited past 5 minutes, and messaged. But it also does not fully establish (iv) to the extent the full track would, and the sample is explicitly thinned. Under NS-1's own terms "a GPS gap that leaves this unproven → escalate", the thinned telemetry is a gap in the continuous-presence evidence.

Given the record as presented, the two NS-1 conditions that can be checked on complete system data (arrival within 200 m, wait past 5 minutes) are satisfied and the driver's cancellation reason is consistent with the record. The rider's claim of coming out "a minute after" cancellation is not corroborated by any app event (no rider-arrival or rider-message event before 13:03:00) and is contradicted by the 6-minute wait the records show. On the balance of the available, system-sourced evidence the $5.00 fee stands.

element_findings.element: driver arrived at pickup within 200 m (NS-1(i))
element_findings.reason: Arrival event logged at 12:57:00 and the GPS fix at that timestamp is ~30 m from the pickup point, inside the 200 m radius.
Wait counted from the later of scheduled pickup and arrival (12:57:00); cancellation at 13:03:00 is 6 minutes later, past the 5-minute free wait.

element_findings.element: driver sent >= 1 in-app message and made >= 1 in-app call before cancelling (NS-1(iii))
element_findings.reason: Two in-app messages precede the 13:03:00 cancellation and one in-app call was placed at 12:58:30; NS-1 requires one message and one call, both present.

element_findings.element: driver remained at the pickup point throughout (NS-1(iv))
element_findings.reason: All fixes from 12:57:30 to 13:03:00 are stationary on Bayfront Avenue within ~3-4 m of each other and within ~30 m of the pickup point; thinned sampling does not show any departure.
Trip data records rider_no_show and the driver's final chat and statement say he cancelled for no-show, matching NS-1/NS-2 rather than NS-3.

rejected_claims.reason: The rider says she came out a minute after cancellation, but no app event (rider arrival, rider message) corroborates this and the records show the driver waited 6 minutes (12:57:00-13:03:00) past the 5-minute free wait, with two messages and a call attempt.
